link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. 旧[[郷社]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|deity=布留多摩命 |本殿=三間社[[流造]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|festival=[[10月5日]]}} '''夜疑神社'''（やぎじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[岸和田市]]にある神社。[[社格]]は旧[[郷社]]。 ==祭神== *[[布留多摩命]] **[[八幡大神]] **[[春日大神]] **[[菅原道真]]　ほか ==歴史== この神社の創建年代等については不詳であるが、[[平安時代]]に作られた[[延喜式]]にも記載されている神社である。平安初期に編纂された[[新撰姓氏録]]に「八木造、和多罪豊玉命の児、布留多摩命の後なり」という記述があり、古代の豪族である[[八木氏]]が祖神である布留多摩命を祀ったのが起源ではないかとされる{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。以前は八木郷の郷社であったが、[[江戸時代]]に各村毎に村社を創設した際には中井村の村社として崇められてきた{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}（古書によると、中井村の「中井」は「中八木」が転訛したものとされる{{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971|p=155}}）。その後、明治に入り[[1872年]]（[[明治]]5年）に村社に列格し、明治41年から42年（[[1908年]]から[[1909年]]）の間に[[八木村 (大阪府)|八木村]]および[[春木町|北掃守村]][[大字]]吉井、[[忠岡町|忠岡村]]大字北出・高月の村社を合祀{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。[[1943年]]（[[昭和]]18年）に郷社に昇格している{{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971|p=155}}。 ==文化財== *岸和田市指定有形文化財 **雨乞絵馬(津田雲渓筆)[https://www.city.kishiwada.osaka.jp/soshiki/70/sitei-bunkazai2015.html 岸和田市内の指定文化財一覧] 岸和田市ホームページ 2016年5月13日閲覧。 *岸和田市指定天然記念物 **夜疑神社社叢 ==例祭等== *例祭 ： 毎年[[10月5日]] *だんじり宮入り ： 毎年[[体育の日]]の前々日 **[[岸和田十月祭礼|八木だんじり祭]]の初日8時半 - 9時半頃にかけて、境内に八木地区（中井町、吉井町、荒木町、下池田町、箕土路町、西大路町、小松里町、額町、額原町、大町、池尻町）の11台の[[だんじり]]が並ぶ。宮入りの順番は毎年同じである{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。 ==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} ==参考文献== * {{Cite |和書|title=岸和田のだんじり |date=2003-09 |publisher=岸和田市観光振興協会 |pages=82 |ref={{SfnRef|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}}}} * {{Cite |和書|title=大阪府神社名鑑 |date=1971-01-22 |publisher=大阪府神道青年会 |pages=155 |ref={{SfnRef|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}}} ==外部リンク== *[http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/ 夜疑神社サイト] - PC版公式サイト *[http://www.yagi-jinja.jp/ 夜疑神社サイト] - スマホ版公式サイト *[http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai12sibu/kisiwada-city/m03_04_kisiwada_yagi.html 大阪府神社庁サイト] {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やきしんしや}} [[Category:大阪府の神社]] [[Category:岸和田市の歴史]] [[Category:大阪府の旧郷社]] [[Category:岸和田市の建築物]]

link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source shrine !domain |- |[[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]] | * 菅原神社（Sugawara-jinja, 下池田字二十四ノ坪） |Sun goddess |- |[[Hachiman|Hachiman]] ([[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]], '''品陀和気命)''' | * 八幡神社（Hachiman-jinja, 荒木字二十四ノ坪） * link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source {{神社 |名称=夜疑神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image=[[File:Yagi Shrine.jpg|250px]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|location=[[大阪府]][[岸和田市]]中井町2-7-1 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|49|N|135|24|14|E|region:JP}} |創建=不詳 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|type=[[式内社]]（小）
旧[[郷社]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|deity=布留多摩命 |本殿=三間社[[流造]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|festival=[[10月5日]]}} '''夜疑神社'''（やぎじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[岸和田市]]にある神社。[[社格]]は旧[[郷社]]。 ==祭神== *[[布留多摩命]] **[[八幡大神]] **[[春日大神]] **[[菅原道真]]　ほか ==歴史== この神社の創建年代等については不詳であるが、[[平安時代]]に作られた[[延喜式]]にも記載されている神社である。平安初期に編纂された[[新撰姓氏録]]に「八木造、和多罪豊玉命の児、布留多摩命の後なり」という記述があり、古代の豪族である[[八木氏]]が祖神である布留多摩命を祀ったのが起源ではないかとされる{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。以前は八木郷の郷社であったが、[[江戸時代]]に各村毎に村社を創設した際には中井村の村社として崇められてきた{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}（古書によると、中井村の「中井」は「中八木」が転訛したものとされる{{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971|p=155}}）。その後、明治に入り[[1872年]]（[[明治]]5年）に村社に列格し、明治41年から42年（[[1908年]]から[[1909年]]）の間に[[八木村 (大阪府)|八木村]]および[[春木町|北掃守村]][[大字]]吉井、[[忠岡町|忠岡村]]大字北出・高月の村社を合祀{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。[[1943年]]（[[昭和]]18年）に郷社に昇格している{{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971|p=155}}。 ==文化財== *岸和田市指定有形文化財 **雨乞絵馬(津田雲渓筆)[https://www.city.kishiwada.osaka.jp/soshiki/70/sitei-bunkazai2015.html 岸和田市内の指定文化財一覧] 岸和田市ホームページ 2016年5月13日閲覧。 *岸和田市指定天然記念物 **夜疑神社社叢 ==例祭等== *例祭 ： 毎年[[10月5日]] *だんじり宮入り ： 毎年[[体育の日]]の前々日 **[[岸和田十月祭礼|八木だんじり祭]]の初日8時半 - 9時半頃にかけて、境内に八木地区（中井町、吉井町、荒木町、下池田町、箕土路町、西大路町、小松里町、額町、額原町、大町、池尻町）の11台の[[だんじり]]が並ぶ。宮入りの順番は毎年同じである{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。 ==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} ==参考文献== * {{Cite |和書|title=岸和田のだんじり |date=2003-09 |publisher=岸和田市観光振興協会 |pages=82 |ref={{SfnRef|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}}}} * {{Cite |和書|title=大阪府神社名鑑 |date=1971-01-22 |publisher=大阪府神道青年会 |pages=155 |ref={{SfnRef|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}}} ==外部リンク== *[http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/ 夜疑神社サイト] - PC版公式サイト *[http://www.yagi-jinja.jp/ 夜疑神社サイト] - スマホ版公式サイト *[http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai12sibu/kisiwada-city/m03_04_kisiwada_yagi.html 大阪府神社庁サイト] {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やきしんしや}} [[Category:大阪府の神社]] [[Category:岸和田市の歴史]] [[Category:大阪府の旧郷社]] [[Category:岸和田市の建築物]] [[Category:getting the categories and imported pages jawiki linked]][[ja:夜疑神社]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:pages of uncertain originality]]

link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. 旧[[郷社]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|deity=布留多摩命 |本殿=三間社[[流造]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|festival=[[10月5日]]}} '''夜疑神社'''（やぎじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[岸和田市]]にある神社。[[社格]]は旧[[郷社]]。 ==祭神== *[[布留多摩命]] '''[[八幡大神]] '''[[春日大神]] '''[[菅原道真]]　ほか ==歴史== この神社の創建年代等については不詳であるが、[[平安時代]]に作られた[[延喜式]]にも記載されている神社である。平安初期に編纂された[[新撰姓氏録]]に「八木造、和多罪豊玉命の児、布留多摩命の後なり」という記述があり、古代の豪族である[[八木氏]]が祖神である布留多摩命を祀ったのが起源ではないかとされる{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。以前は八木郷の郷社であったが、[[江戸時代]]に各村毎に村社を創設した際には中井村の村社として崇められてきた{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}（古書によると、中井村の「中井」は「中八木」が転訛したものとされる{{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971|p=155}}）。その後、明治に入り[[1872年]]（[[明治]]5年）に村社に列格し、明治41年から42年（[[1908年]]から[[1909年]]）の間に[[八木村 (大阪府)|八木村]]および[[春木町|北掃守村]][[大字]]吉井、[[忠岡町|忠岡村]]大字北出・高月の村社を合祀{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。[[1943年]]（[[昭和]]18年）に郷社に昇格している{{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971|p=155}}。 ==文化財== *岸和田市指定有形文化財 '''雨乞絵馬(津田雲渓筆)[https://www.city.kishiwada.osaka.jp/soshiki/70/sitei-bunkazai2015.html 岸和田市内の指定文化財一覧] 岸和田市ホームページ 2016年5月13日閲覧。 *岸和田市指定天然記念物 '''夜疑神社社叢 ==例祭等== *例祭 ： 毎年[[10月5日]] *だんじり宮入り ： 毎年[[体育の日]]の前々日 '''[[岸和田十月祭礼|八木だんじり祭]]の初日8時半 - 9時半頃にかけて、境内に八木地区（中井町、吉井町、荒木町、下池田町、箕土路町、西大路町、小松里町、額町、額原町、大町、池尻町）の11台の[[だんじり]]が並ぶ。宮入りの順番は毎年同じである{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993|p=82}}。 ==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} ==参考文献== * {{Cite |和書|title=岸和田のだんじり |date=2003-09 |publisher=岸和田市観光振興協会 |pages=82 |ref={{SfnRef|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}}}} * {{Cite |和書|title=大阪府神社名鑑 |date=1971-01-22 |publisher=大阪府神道青年会 |pages=155 |ref={{SfnRef|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}}} ==外部リンク== *[http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/ 夜疑神社サイト] - PC版公式サイト *[http://www.yagi-jinja.jp/ 夜疑神社サイト] - スマホ版公式サイト *[http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai12sibu/kisiwada-city/m03_04_kisiwada_yagi.html 大阪府神社庁サイト] {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やきしんしや}} [[Category:大阪府の神社]] [[Category:岸和田市の歴史]] [[Category:大阪府の旧郷社]] [[Category:岸和田市の建築物]] [[Category:getting the categories and imported pages jawiki linked]][[ja:夜疑神社]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:pages of uncertain originality]] [[Category:pages of uncertain originality]]

link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety.
