also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities. {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} of the [[Kujūku Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. [[fr:Yagi-jinja]] [[Category:dd]][[ja:夜疑神社]] [[Category:dd]][[en:draft:Yagi Shrine]] == {{ill|Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子}} == {{Main|{{ill|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子}}}}The {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Kujūku Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kōdō|ja|熊野古道}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Kujūku Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|ja|久米田駅}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|ja|阪和線}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子}} → '''{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|fr|Yagi-jinja|lt=Ikeda Ōji|error=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Asokawa Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kogi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' → {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}} == Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}} The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-mikoto|fr|Furutama}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety.
