link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. [[Kishiwada, Osaka|Kishiwada, Osaka]].{{Cite link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[Meiji period]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. {{ill|Inokuchi Ōji|ja|井ノ口王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuchi Ōji|qq=}} → link to Miyamoto Musashi.https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine == History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period. Several shrines were merged with it during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in [[:en:1943|1943]]. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}} It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years. == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji (99 Ōji Shrines)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kōdō]], especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano. Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]], many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era. This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka. Located near [[:en:Kumeda Station|Kumeda Station]] on the [[:en:Hanwa Line|Hanwa Line]], the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada.
