{{Infobox religious building|name=Yagi Shrine|native_name=夜疑神社|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:Yagi Shrine Torii.jpg|map_type=Japan|coordinates={{Coord|34.480278|N|135.403889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}|deity={{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|WD=Q106241380}} |kk=|location={{ill|Kishiwada|WD=Q740456}}|architecture_style={{ill|nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684}} |image=Yagi Shrine Torii closeup.jpg }}
{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>
There is a children's library on the shrine grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-26|title=��^�_�Ђ̎�������|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626222624/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/woody.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is known fo its link to Miyamoto Musashi.<ref>https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine</ref>
== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.

== Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016">{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />
During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /> {| {{Infobox religious building|name=Yagi Shrine|native_name=夜疑神社|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:Yagi Shrine Torii.jpg|map_type=Japan|coordinates={{Coord|34.480278|N|135.403889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}|deity={{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|WD=Q106241380|1=Furutama-no-Mikoto}} |kk=|location={{ill|Kishiwada|WD=Q740456|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}|architecture_style={{ill|nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |image=Yagi Shrine Torii closeup.jpg }}
{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>
There is a children's library on the shrine grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-26|title=��^�_�Ђ̎�������|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626222624/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/woody.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is known fo its link to Miyamoto Musashi.<ref>https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine</ref>
== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.

== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.

{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>

== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. {{Infobox religious building|name=Yagi Shrine|native_name=夜疑神社|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:Yagi Shrine Torii.jpg|map_type=Japan|coordinates={{Coord|34.480278|N|135.403889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}|deity={{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|WD=Q106241380|1=Furutama-no-Mikoto}} |kk=|location={{ill|Kishiwada|WD=Q740456|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}|architecture_style={{ill|nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |image=Yagi Shrine Torii closeup.jpg }}
{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>
There is a children's library on the shrine grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-26|title=��^�_�Ђ̎�������|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626222624/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/woody.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is known fo its link to Miyamoto Musashi.<ref>https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine</ref>
== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.

== Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016">{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />
During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /> {| class="wikitable" |+ !deity !Source shrine !domain |- |[[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]] | * 菅原神社（Sugawara-jinja, 下池田字二十四ノ坪） |Sun goddess |- |[[Hachiman|Hachiman]] ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>
There is a children's library on the shrine grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-26|title=��^�_�Ђ̎�������|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626222624/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/woody.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is known fo its link to Miyamoto Musashi.<ref>https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine</ref>
== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. {{Infobox religious building|name=Yagi Shrine|native_name=夜疑神社|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:Yagi Shrine Torii.jpg|map_type=Japan|coordinates={{Coord|34.480278|N|135.403889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}|deity={{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|WD=Q106241380|1=Furutama-no-Mikoto}} |kk=|location={{ill|Kishiwada|WD=Q740456|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}|architecture_style={{ill|nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |image=Yagi Shrine Torii closeup.jpg }}
{{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>
There is a children's library on the shrine grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-26|title=��^�_�Ђ̎�������|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626222624/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/woody.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is known fo its link to Miyamoto Musashi.<ref>https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine</ref>
== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.

== Enshrined deities == The shrine has many kami enshrined in it.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016">{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�_�Ђ̌�Ր_|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202730/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/saijin.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
The main deity is {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} the God of exorcism and traffic safety.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />
During the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|Shrine Consolidation Policy]] many shrines were merged into this one, so it worships a very large amount of deities.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /> {| {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|simple|User:Yagi Shrine|en|Draft:Yagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} (夜疑神社) is the shrine of the {{ill|Yagi clan|ja|八木氏|fr|Clan Yagi|en:draft|8=simple|9=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi clan|qq=}}<ref name="www.norichan.jp" /> it worships {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2016" /><ref name="www.norichan.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社|url=http://www.norichan.jp/jinja/benkyou2/yagi.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=www.norichan.jp}}</ref>
It has a [[Chinju no Mori|Chinju no Mori]] around it.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�Ђ̋����U��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828023607/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/sanpo.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is located at {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|en|Kishiwada, Osaka|WD=Q740456|lt=Kishiwada, Osaka|1=Kishiwada, Osaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-18|title=��^�i�€�j�_��|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818202710/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/index.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is accessible from {{ill|Tadaoka Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadaoka Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nankai Main Line|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-28|title=��^�_�ЁE���ē�|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828025755/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/mitiannai.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp">{{Cite web|title=夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>
There is a children's library on the shrine grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-26|title=��^�_�Ђ̎�������|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626222624/http://orange.zero.jp/hara.park/woody.html|access-date=2024-03-23|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
It is known fo its link to Miyamoto Musashi.<ref>https://www.es-kyoto.yumeyakata.com/single-post/2018/02/08/the-statue-of-miyamoto-musashi-at-yagi-shrine</ref>
== History == The year this shrine was founded is unknown, but it is also mentioned in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki]], which was created during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=御由緒 {{!}} 夜疑神社【大阪府岸和田市】交通安全・厄除け祈願|url=https://www.yagi-jinja.jp/about/|access-date=2024-03-23|website=www.yagi-jinja.jp}}</ref>. In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}} compiled in the early Heian period, there is a description indicates that the Yagi clan, an ancient powerful clan, enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja|布留多摩命|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Furutama|8=en|9=Draft:Furutama-no-Mikoto|fr|Furutama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furutama-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} .
The Shrine is associated with {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} of the [[Ninety-Nine Ōji]]. It was located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada. The shrine was believed to be associated with {{ill|Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekigawa Shrine (Kishiwada)|qq=}} and was merged into {{ill|Yagi Shrine|ja|夜疑神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period.
Several shrines were merged with it during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} <ref name="web.archive.org-2016" />{{Sfn|岸和田市観光振興協会|1993}} . It was promoted to Go-sha in {{ill|1943|en|1943|WD=Q18623|lt=1943|1=1943}}. {{Sfn|大阪府神道青年会|1971}}
It was rennovated in 2013 for the first time in 350 years.<ref name="www.yagi-jinja.jp" /> == {{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Kaizuka)|lt=Ikeda Ōji|ja|池田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda Ōji|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)}} == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}The {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (99 Ōji Shrines)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} shrines refer to a group of sacred sites along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kōdō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} route, established during the 12th and 13th centuries by {{ill|Kumano Shugendō|ja|熊野修験|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135493040|1=Kumano Shugendo}} practitioners. These shrines served to protect pilgrims, including members of the imperial family and nobility, on their journeys to the sacred sites of Kumano.
Following the decline of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}} after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, many of these shrines fell into disrepair. Despite some restoration efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}, many shrines were lost due to urbanization and the State Shinto reforms of the Meiji era.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kishiwada and Kaizuka.
Located near {{ill|Kumeda Station|en|Kumeda Station|WD=Q857003|lt=Kumeda Station|1=Kumeda Station}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|WD=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line|1=Hanwa Line}}, the former site of Ikeda Ōji is now private land in Shimo-Ikeda, Kishiwada.
